sourcedFrom: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. (UNDATED — nothing in the document states one)
cleanIntro:
The Sabre is printed titanium and Inconel, and the book treats the core as closed: it prints no baffle procedure at all. What it does publish is the part that actually gets dirty in a way you can reach — the threaded socket and sealing taper in the back of the can, and the fast-attach or direct-thread mount that lives in it. Those two surfaces are what hold the can square on the barrel, so the whole routine is about keeping them clean, greased and undamaged.

One book covers both the Sabre 556 and the Sabre Mixtape, and its mounting, removal and cleaning pages are printed once, for the series.

steps.title: Host safe before the can is touched
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction. Magazine out, chamber emptied and looked into, safety on SAFE — on the host, using the host's own manual for how.
steps.prose: Removing a can means your hand goes around the muzzle, so the host is made safe first, every time. This book covers the suppressor, not the gun it is on — for how to unload your particular host, it sends you to that firearm's own manual.
steps.quote: Render the firearm safe by removing the magazine, completely unloading the firearm and engaging the safety mechanism to the “SAFE” position.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Removing a Sabre Suppressor from a host firearm, printed p.21

steps.title: Let it come down to room temperature
steps.action: Touch-test from a distance first. If it is warm at all, leave it on the host and walk away until it is not.
steps.prose: A can holds heat long after the barrel feels cool, and the book will not let cleaning start on a hot one either.
steps.quote: Verify the suppressor is at ambient temperature. If the suppressor is hot, allow it to cool.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Removing a Sabre Suppressor from a host firearm, printed p.21
steps.warn: Never handle a hot suppressor without heat-resistant gloves, as this may lead to skin burns and/or personal injury.

steps.title: Unscrew the can off the muzzle device
steps.action: Grip the body of the suppressor firmly and turn it counter-clockwise off the muzzle device threads.
steps.prose: It was torqued on, so expect the first quarter-turn to take effort. Grip the tube, not anything that might be loose.
steps.quote: While firmly grasping the suppressor, unscrew the suppressor from the muzzle device threads in a counter clockwise direction as indicated in figure 8.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Removing a Sabre Suppressor from a host firearm, printed p.21

steps.title: Spanner the mount out of the can
steps.action: With the can off the gun, put a spanner on the fast-attach adapter, break it loose, then unthread it the rest of the way by hand.
steps.prose: This is the only part the book has you take out. The book's own cleaning step 1 is exactly this: if a fast-attach or direct-thread mount is in the can, it comes out first. These instructions are for the Plan B fast-attach adapter; if your can carries another maker's adapter, this book does not cover it — use that maker's removal instructions.
steps.quote: To remove a fast-attach adapter from a dismounted Sabre Suppressor use a spanner to break loose the fast-attach adapter and unthread it and remove it by hand.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Configuring a Sabre Suppressor for fast-attach use, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ That is the whole strip
steps.action: Can and mount are now two pieces, and that is as far as it goes. Do not try to open the tube or push anything into the core to loosen it.
steps.prose: The book's cleaning section stops at the mount and the exterior, and its warnings page forbids going further.
steps.quote: Never disassemble, alter, or modify your suppressor beyond what is outlined in this manual.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — WARNINGS — Modifications, printed p.8

steps.title: Scrub the socket and taper in the back of the can
steps.action: Gun-cleaning brush and solvent into the rear of the suppressor: work the threaded socket and the tapered sealing surface until both are clean.
steps.prose: The taper is a seal, not just a guide — carbon left on it holds the mount off-square, and that is where a baffle strike starts.
steps.quote: Using a gun cleaning brush and solvent, thoroughly scrub the threaded socket and taper in the rear of the suppressor.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — CLEANING THE SABRE SUPPRESSOR SERIES, printed p.22
steps.warn: Always wear protective gear, such as eye protection and solvent-resistant gloves when working with any solvent.

steps.title: Inspect the socket and taper
steps.action: With it clean, look at the threads and the sealing taper in the rear of the can. You are looking for a clean, undamaged surface — no galling, no burr, nothing left in the root of the threads.
steps.prose: A damaged socket is not something to thread a mount into and hope.
steps.quote: Inspect the threaded socket and tapered sealing surface in the rear of the suppressor to ensure they are clean and free of damage.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Configuring a Sabre Suppressor for fast-attach use, printed p.18

steps.title: Clean the mount's outside threads and taper
steps.action: Same treatment on the fast-attach or direct-thread mount: its outside threads and its taper are the other half of the seal.
steps.prose: Then inspect them the same way — clean and free of damage.
steps.quote: Clean the threads and taper on the outside of the fast-attach or direct thread mount.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — CLEANING THE SABRE SUPPRESSOR SERIES, printed p.22

steps.title: Wipe the outside down
steps.action: A clean cloth over the exterior of the can.
steps.prose: That is the last cleaning step the book prints.
steps.quote: Wipe off the exterior of the suppressor with a clean cloth.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — CLEANING THE SABRE SUPPRESSOR SERIES, printed p.22

steps.title: Grease the mount and thread it back in
steps.action: A small amount of high-temperature grease or anti-seize on the mount's threads and taper, then thread it into the rear of the can.
steps.prose: The grease is what lets the spanner break it loose next time.
steps.quote: to the threads and taper on the fast-attach or direct thread mount and reinstall the mount in the rear of the suppressor
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — CLEANING THE SABRE SUPPRESSOR SERIES, printed p.22
steps.warn: Never attempt to install an adapter in a Sabre Suppressor with threads or tapered sealing surfaces that are dirty or damaged, as this may lead to property damage, personal injury and/or death.

steps.title: Seat the taper, then spanner it tight
steps.action: Thread it in until the mount's outer taper seats against the taper inside the can, then tighten it with a spanner.
steps.prose: Seated on the taper is the point — threads alone do not center it.
steps.quote: Use a spanner to tighten the fast-attach mount into the suppressor.
steps.cite: Sabre Suppressor OWNERS MANUAL — SABRE SUPPRESSOR MANUAL (title printed on the back cover). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Configuring a Sabre Suppressor for fast-attach use, printed p.18

deepAbsentReason: The book's cleaning section (printed p.22) ends at the mount and the exterior of the can: it removes the mount, scrubs the rear socket and taper, cleans the mount, greases and reinstalls it, and wipes the outside. It prints no baffle, core or end-cap procedure for either model, and its Modifications warning (printed p.8) forbids disassembly beyond what the manual outlines. There is nothing deeper published.

cleaning.name: REAR SOCKET AND TAPER
tasks: Threaded socket in the rear of the can scrubbed with brush and solvent
Tapered sealing surface scrubbed the same way
Both inspected — clean and free of damage
⛔ Only on a can that is off the gun and at room temperature

cleaning.name: THE MOUNT
tasks: Outside threads and taper of the fast-attach or direct-thread mount cleaned
Inspected — clean and free of damage
Small amount of high-temperature grease or anti-seize on threads and taper before it goes back

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Outside of the can wiped with a clean cloth

cleaning.name: ⛔ LEAVE ALONE
tasks: Do not open the tube or work on the core — the book prints no procedure for it
Do not fit parts not made or authorized by Palmetto State Armory

reassembly: Mount greased on its threads and taper, threaded into the rear of the can until its taper seats, and tightened with a spanner.
Look through the can from the rear: the bullet path must be clear.
Check the can over for any sign of damage.
Host made safe again — magazine out, empty, safety on SAFE — and the muzzle device threads and tapers cleaned.
Screw the can on clockwise until the rear of the mount sits flush and square against the shoulder, and torque it to 10 ft lbs.
Confirm alignment with an alignment rod before firing.
fncheck: Palmetto State Armory's book does not print a function check for the can. Its mounting pages close on two checks before use: look through the suppressor from the rear to see the bullet path is unobstructed, and confirm alignment with an alignment rod once it is torqued on.
